title: Collaboration: Resume a Conversation After Disconnection
businessContext: A laptop reconnects after a long outage. Blindly replaying the latest page loses messages, while an expired cursor silently hides history.
problemStatement: Implement solution({ cursor, highWater, retainedFrom, limit, events }). Inputs are valid safe integers: 0 <= cursor, 0 <= highWater, 1 <= retainedFrom <= highWater+1, limit >= 1. events is the ascending contiguous retained log with seq retainedFrom through highWater. Return { status, events, nextCursor, hasMore }. cursor > highWater => invalid_cursor with empty events and unchanged cursor. cursor < retainedFrom-1 => reset with empty events and nextCursor=highWater; obtain a separate snapshot before continuing. Otherwise return up to limit events strictly after cursor, status ok, nextCursor=last returned seq or cursor, hasMore=nextCursor<highWater. Error/reset hasMore is false.
constraints: Implement the synchronous solution(input) contract exactly. Do not mutate input; all inputs are JSON data.
This is a deterministic state model. It does not open sockets, send notifications, authorize real users, or establish media connections.
candidateTasks: Reproduce the starter failure, implement the invariant, and pass every authored case.
How would you atomically capture a snapshot/high-water pair and handle a connection dropping before acknowledgement?

testCases.name: Already caught up does not replay last message
Empty log has a stable zero cursor

hints: Write down validation and replay precedence before changing state.
Use stable IDs and monotonic sequence/version values; preserve input ownership.
alternativeApproaches: Use an append-only event log with transactional projections.
Use a database snapshot plus a versioned resume cursor.
commonMistakes: Trusting delivery order or treating retries as new operations.
Mutating caller-owned arrays or accepting cross-channel data.
Presenting a fixture result as a guarantee of real-time delivery or media connectivity.
